text: In Aztec legend, something lived in the deep water. They called it the Ahuizotl.
One night, a fisherman walking home along the lake heard a baby crying.
Out in the reeds. Alone. In the dark.
He called out, and the crying stopped.
Then it started again. Closer to the water.
He knelt at the edge. The reeds were moving.
He reached in, and a small hand grabbed his wrist.
Not a baby's hand. It grew from the end of a long, black tail.
The water closed over him, and the lake went quiet.
The Aztecs warned: if you hear a baby crying by the water at night, don't go to it. It isn't a baby.
